Standard diagnostics for a fit, or for every candidate of a comparison

Source: R/diagnose.R
diagnose.Rd

Runs the A/E diagnostics of a fitted model over the experience data it was fitted to, broken down however you ask, and returns them alongside the model's coefficient table and correlation matrix. Given a model_comparison, it does so for every converged candidate, not just the winner, and the whole set crosses the data once.

A fit keeps no data, which is why the data is passed again here rather than remembered. What the fit does keep is what it was run with – its include, weight, relevance, overdispersion and time scale – and those are the defaults, so the diagnostics of a fit are by default over the same population, weighted the same way, as the fit itself.

Usage

diagnose(
  exp_data,
  x,
  breakdown = NULL,
  include,
  weight,
  val_relevance,
  val_distance,
  settings = NULL,
  overdispersion = NULL,
  time_scale = NULL,
  threads = cpp_veil_default_threads()
)

is_diagnosis(x)

# S3 method for class 'diagnosis'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'diagnosis'
plot(x, ...)

Arguments

exp_data

The experience data, ordinarily the data the model was fitted to.

x

A fit or a model_comparison. A lone fit is one candidate, labelled by its model's name where it has one and fit otherwise.

breakdown

An include, an includes(), a list of either, or NULL. See Breakdowns.

include

The population. Defaults to the one the fit was run over.

weight, val_relevance, val_distance

Pronoun expressions, as in aev(). Each defaults to what the fit was run with; give NULL to run without.

settings, overdispersion, time_scale

As in aev(). Each defaults to the fit's own.

threads

The number of worker threads.

...

For plot(), passed to autoplot.aev() for every chart, except title and subtitle, which name the candidate and the breakdown.

Value

diagnose() returns a diagnosis, whose fields are candidates (one entry per converged candidate, best first, each holding summary – the summary() of its fit – and aev, a list of one aev() per breakdown), breakdowns (the breakdown labels), labels (the include and weight the diagnostics were run with, as text), overdispersion, and pv_impact, which is NULL until present-value impacts exist.

plot() draws the chart grid and returns x invisibly.

Breakdowns

breakdown may be a single include or includes(), or a list of them for several breakdowns side by side. Each gives one aev() per candidate, with one record per element. A list's names label the breakdowns; unnamed ones are labelled by what was written. NULL gives one ungrouped A/E per candidate.

What it shows

print() gives each candidate's coefficient table and correlation matrix, then each of its A/E tables. plot() draws a grid of A/E charts, candidates down the page and breakdowns across it, each drawn by autoplot.aev().

Examples

data <- exp_data(
  list(
    birth     = datey::datey(c(1945, 1950, 1955, 1940, 1948, 1952, 1938, 1960, 1943)),
    male      = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE),
    sex       = c("m", "f", "m", "f", "m", "m", "f", "m", "f"),
    E2R_start = datey::datey(rep(2015, 9)),
    E2R_end   = datey::datey(c(2020, 2018, 2020, 2019, 2020, 2020, 2020, 2017, 2020)),
    E2R_died  = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE)
  ),
  exp_start = datey::datey(2015),
  exp_end   = datey::datey(2020)
)

reference <- gompertz_mortality(slope_t = 0)
comparison <- compare_models(
  data,
  list(level = model(reference, covariates(level = 1)),
       sex   = model(reference, covariates(male = .i$male, female = !.i$male))),
  overdispersion = 1
)

d <- diagnose(data, comparison,
              breakdown = list(sex = categories(.i$sex, "m", "f"), age = ages(55, 85, by = 15)))
d
